clue.text: King not returning for a dance

parts.note: Charles is the name of several English kings

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A monarch declines to come back for a ball, staying away from the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not returning' reads like 'not coming back', but 'returning' is the reversal signal acting on the word 'not' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s jazz-age dance with swinging kicks.

clue.text: Prison in constant decline

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics (the speed of light)
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: An inmate's life behind bars is one of steady, unending deterioration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure for confining someone, so it serves loosely as a word for a jail.

clue.text: Assistant in a small company — bright, it's said

parts.note: Co. is the short form of company

indicators.note: tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: bright means giving out light

explanation.surface: A clever helper works for a little firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' gives LYTE, which sounds like LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an attendant or helper, originally one who assists a priest at the altar.

clue.text: Squirearchy's got good record

parts.note: to land something is to get or secure it, so landed means got
an entry is an item recorded in a log or register

explanation.surface: The country squires have acquired a fine reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'has'; it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The squirearchy is the class of country landowners, which is what the landed gentry are.

clue.text: Sorry tale of old boy on board, right-winger

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside it, so these letters go inside the ship's letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS stands for steamship
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A sad yarn about a former pupil who sailed with a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a pitiful account meant to win sympathy, a tale of woe.

clue.text: English actor I dismissed — Reed, perhaps

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Laurence Olivier was a great English stage and screen actor

explanation.surface: One English actor is dropped from a film and replaced by another named Reed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes I from OLIVIER. Oliver Reed was a hellraising English film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is the first name of actor Oliver Reed, so the definition is given by example.

clue.text: Turn left following game

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer left after a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs and balls over a course of holes.

clue.text: Manage to perform surgery

definitions.meaning: to ... a business or machine is to run or manage it

explanation.surface: Advice to a hospital chief about cutting both budgets and patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Operate covers both running something and carrying out a surgical procedure.

clue.text: Trembling, say, in cast

indicators.note: tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to fling something is to cast or throw it
to utter is to say aloud

explanation.surface: An actor in a play's company shakes as they deliver a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttering describes quick quivering movement, like a nervous tremble.

clue.text: This may attract fish — crumbled a bit at sea

parts.note: something ground has been crushed or crumbled

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Breaking up a little bait and throwing it in the ocean draws in fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges A BIT into BAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbait is food scattered in water by anglers to lure fish to a spot.

clue.text: List of utensils initially taken by workers

indicators.note: the first piece is taken by the second, which comes before it

parts.note: men can mean workers, as in management and men

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An inventory of kitchen tools is grabbed first by the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes, or of options on a screen.

clue.text: Professional brought off

definitions.meaning: an ... performer is skilled and expert
something ... has been achieved or carried out

explanation.surface: An expert pulled it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished means both highly skilled and successfully completed.

clue.text: Sort to use a keyboard, maybe

definitions.meaning: to write with keys; maybe since a typewriter would do too

explanation.surface: A sort of instruction to get typing.
explanation.definitionFit: Type means both a kind or category and to press keys to write text.

clue.text: Incisive, a new leader of team by ditch

parts.note: a trench is a ditch

indicators.note: the leader is the one in front, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A sharp new captain stands beside a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places TRENCH next to the rest, which comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means cutting and forceful, as incisive remarks are.

clue.text: Set off with southern colleague on Scottish river

parts.note: an ally is a partner or colleague
the Forth is a river flowing into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Starting out on a Scottish river with a partner from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally forth is to set out boldly on a journey or venture.

clue.text: Makes allegations about English righters of wrongs?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to aver is to assert or allege

explanation.surface: Someone accuses the English of being self-appointed fixers of injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: Avengers punish wrongdoing, setting wrongs right by retribution; the question mark marks the loose sense.

clue.text: Definitely not old, female in close

indicators.note: tells us these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: near means close

explanation.surface: An old woman nearby flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is an informal British exclamation of refusal, like 'certainly not'.

clue.text: Great, a joke I fed to MC

indicators.note: material fed to someone goes into them, so these letters go inside

parts.note: taken as written, the master of ceremonies
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A comedian hands a gag to the compère, who calls it great.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means grand and impressive, a sense of great.

clue.text: Celebrity on edge

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an end is an edge or extremity

explanation.surface: A famous person is feeling nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is someone famous and admired, as in a living legend.

clue.text: Information involving son and daughter makes one cheer

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a lad is a boy or son

explanation.surface: News about one's children brings happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden someone is to make them happy, the transitive sense of cheer.

clue.text: Military operation in barracks — a GI recalled name

parts.note: a camp is a military base, like barracks

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: An American soldier in barracks remembered the name of a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns GI into IG. GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a series of military operations aimed at one objective.

clue.text: Acceptable batting arrangement

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
an order is an arrangement or sequence

explanation.surface: A cricket line-up that passes muster.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting order is the sequence in which players bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In order means proper or permissible, as in 'is that in order?'.

clue.text: Warns suspect, describing magistrate's last solution

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so these letters surround the other
suspect means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are rearranged
the last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A suspect is cautioned and given the magistrate's final verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges WARNS into ANSWR; 'describing' puts it round E, the end of magistrate ('s only links).
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is the solution to a puzzle or problem.

clue.text: Notoriousness of convict in European country

indicators.note: tells us the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
a lag, usually old lag, is British slang for a convict

explanation.surface: The scandal of a prisoner held in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrance is the quality of being glaringly obvious or notorious, as with flagrant wrongdoing.

clue.text: Highly loved person not wanting to work, we hear

indicators.note: tells us to go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: idle means lazy, unwilling to work

explanation.surface: A darling of the public turns out to be work-shy, rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone adored or worshipped by fans.

clue.text: Responsibility deacon usually carries

indicators.note: the phrase carries the answer within it, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Church duty that falls to a deacon as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the burden or duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Sit on note including papers

indicators.note: including means holding within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Sitting on a memo with documents attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a horse or bike is to sit on it while it moves.

clue.text: Turned the ignition key with it?

definitions.meaning: a car is ... with the ignition key
slang for alert and trendy, with it

explanation.surface: Did a driver start the car with the key?
explanation.definitionFit: Switched on means both started up and, informally, sharp and fashionable.

clue.text: Husband with influence

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: A man whose spouse carries sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a hand in something is to have influence or a part in it.

clue.text: Gets across editor's methods

indicators.note: something lying across another spans it, so these letters go round the second piece

parts.note: to procure is to get or obtain
ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Getting the editor's ways of doing things understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedures are established ways of doing things, that is methods.
